inputs.text: Israel's parliament kicked off a debate today on a bill that would make the death penalty the automatic punishment for any West Bank Palestinian convicted of murdering Israelis. Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir is the one driving this and framing it as a victory for accountability, but it's clear this is just another move to lock in systemic discrimination and inequality. It's zeroing in on vulnerable Palestinian communities with these extreme measures while completely ignoring the structural roots of the violence—entrenched power imbalances and generations of historical oppression. Opponents are right to call it out as racist and draconian, because it does nothing to achieve real justice or save lives. Instead, it props up the status quo by hammering marginalized groups rather than pushing the institutional reforms needed to tackle inequality across the board.
